resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and Arabic source scope, review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review metadata, queue validation, typecheck, 79 test files with 462 tests, complete build, 39 IIS rules with 61 route cases, and 724 generated-link checks passed.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded Arabic pass identified 25 actionable terminology, formula, and unit defects in electrical, circuit, trigonometric, thermal, and SI content; all 25 were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent Arabic human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted.

findings.summary: The electrical-power title used the Arabic word for energy rather than power.
evidence: The previous title was ‘الطاقة الكهربائية’ although the section defines P in watts.

findings.summary: The Joule-heating summary said current converts resistance into heat.
evidence: Electrical energy, not resistance, is converted into heat.
findings.resolution: Changed the object of conversion to electrical energy.

findings.summary: The heating paragraph used an awkward description of energy changing temperature.
evidence: The previous Arabic phrasing said energy changes ‘to’ temperature.
findings.resolution: Rephrased the relation between energy, temperature, and surface transfer.

findings.summary: The series-cell formula retained English text.
evidence: The formula ended with ‘(series)’.

findings.summary: The parallel-cell formula retained English text.
evidence: The formula ended with ‘(parallel)’.

findings.summary: The TCR worked-example title was an incorrect literal phrase.
evidence: The previous title was ‘عملت المثال’.

findings.summary: The TCR coefficient formula contained a corrupted degree unit.
evidence: The previous formula ended with ‘Å’.

findings.summary: The temperature-change formula contained a corrupted degree character.
evidence: The previous expression ended with a control-character rendering.

findings.summary: The TCR conclusion contained a corrupted temperature unit.
evidence: The previous conclusion included ‘20 = درجة مئوية’.

findings.summary: The trigonometry explanation mislabeled sine as cosine.
evidence: The paragraph named جيب التمام for both the opposite and adjacent ratios.
findings.resolution: Rewrote the SOH-CAH-TOA explanation with sine, cosine, and tangent correctly assigned.

findings.summary: The right-triangle setup used an awkward literal construction.
evidence: The previous text said the hypotenuse ‘meets’ an angle.
findings.resolution: Rephrased it as a 10 cm hypotenuse forming a 30° angle.

findings.summary: The opposite-side formula mixed Arabic function notation with a translated label.
evidence: The previous expression used جا and Arabic words inside a protected worked formula.
findings.resolution: Restored the standard opposite-side expression with sin and metric units.

findings.summary: The adjacent-side formula mixed localized notation with an inconsistent unit style.
evidence: The previous expression used كوس and Arabic unit wording.
findings.resolution: Restored the standard adjacent-side expression with cos and centimetres.

findings.summary: The sine formula retained English geometry terms inconsistently with the Arabic prose.
evidence: The formula did not use the protected standard expression used by the other locale contracts.

findings.summary: The cosine formula retained English geometry terms inconsistently.
evidence: The cosine expression was not aligned with the corrected technical notation.

findings.summary: The tangent formula retained English geometry terms inconsistently.
evidence: The tangent expression was not aligned with the corrected technical notation.

findings.summary: The heat-capacity display name used the word for power capacity.
evidence: The previous display name was ‘القدرة الحرارية’, which conflicts with thermal capacity.

findings.summary: The heat-capacity worked-example title was an incorrect literal phrase.
evidence: The previous title was ‘عملت المثال’.

findings.summary: The heat-capacity conclusion used an unnatural requirement phrase.
evidence: The previous wording described an ideal energy requirement rather than required energy.
findings.resolution: Rephrased the conclusion as ideal energy required and real-heater losses.

findings.summary: The electrical-heating worked formula used Arabic letters and units in place of protected symbols.
evidence: The previous expression used ‘ر’ and Arabic watt/joule words.
findings.resolution: Restored the protected t, J, and W notation.

findings.summary: The heat-flux worked-example title was an incorrect literal phrase.
evidence: The previous title was ‘عملت المثال’.

findings.summary: The heat-flux worked formula localized protected units inconsistently.
evidence: The previous expression used Arabic watt abbreviations and omitted standard grouping.
findings.resolution: Restored the protected W and m² notation with grouped thousands.

findings.summary: The practical-checks title was mistranslated as checks in an inappropriate sense.
evidence: The previous title was ‘الشيكات العملية’.

findings.summary: The practical heat-flux bullet used an incomplete imperative construction.
evidence: The previous bullet began with a bare noun-like form ‘التمييز’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to a direct imperative distinguishing average and local heat flux.

findings.summary: Several SI base-unit rows contained incorrect Arabic quantity names, symbols, or unit names.
evidence: The rows used قداس, ثانيا, الخلد, and قرص مضغوط for mass, time, amount, and luminous intensity.
findings.resolution: Corrected the rows to الكتلة/kg, الزمن/s, مول/mol, and شدة الإضاءة/cd.
